title: Write-ahead logging and crash recovery
brief: Log a transaction, commit it, checkpoint it, and recover correctly from a power cut after every single write.
hints: A block is 16 bytes. TxBegin is b'B' + bytes([txid, n]) + bytes(addrs), padded with .ljust(16, b'\0'). Decoding is the reverse: check the first byte, then read the next ones.
The commit is the single write of TxEnd. Every data block must already be in the journal before you write it, or recovery could replay garbage.
Journal slots: TxBegin at block 0, data copy i at block 1 + i, TxEnd at block 1 + n. Use sorted(updates) so the order is the same every time.
recover decides with one test: is there a TxBegin at block 0, and is block 1 + n a TxEnd with the same txid? Only then copy the journal blocks to their home addresses.
Recovery must be safe to run again. Copying the same journal blocks to the same home blocks twice does no harm, and freeing the log is the last step.
